title: Taxation of Digital Transactions
outcomes: Describe e-commerce models and features of the digital economy.
Identify tax challenges of digitalisation and India's response.
Compute tax on transfer of virtual digital assets.
Apply TDS and gift provisions to virtual digital assets.

meta.exam_tip: Compute VDA gains token by token and state that losses are ignored.

concepts.title: Digital economy and e-commerce models
body: Section 402(12) defines electronic commerce as supply of goods, services or both, including digital products, over a digital or electronic network. Models include B2B, B2C, C2C and platform-based marketplaces, subscription services, digital wallets and the sharing economy.
Features of digital business: mobility of intangibles and users, reliance on data and network effects, multi-sided platforms, and the ability to serve a market with little or no physical presence.
Digital wallets and mobile money enable trusted online payments, widening access for people without traditional banking.
concepts.analogy: Value is created where users and data are, not only where offices are.
concepts.work: A ride-hailing app matches drivers and riders without owning cars.

concepts.title: Tax challenges of digitalisation
body: Key issues: nexus (PE rules based on physical presence weaken), data and user-created value, characterisation of payments (business income, royalty or fees for technical services), and allocation of profits between jurisdictions.
BEPS Action 1 considered a significant economic presence test, withholding tax on digital transactions and an equalisation levy; the OECD/G20 Two-Pillar solution followed.

India introduced a 6% equalisation levy on specified online advertising services (2016) and extended it to e-commerce supplies (2020); the e-commerce levy was withdrawn from 1 August 2024 and the levy on specified digital services was abolished by the Finance Act, 2025.
concepts.analogy: Tax rules built for factories struggle with platforms.
concepts.work: An overseas ad platform with Indian users but no office tests PE rules.

concepts.title: Taxation of virtual digital assets
body: Virtual digital asset (section 2(111)) covers information, code, number or token generated cryptographically or otherwise that provides a digital representation of value, including crypto-assets on distributed ledgers and non-fungible tokens as notified; Indian and foreign currency and gift cards or vouchers are excluded.

Income from transfer of a VDA is taxed at 30% (section 194(1) Table Sl. No. 4) regardless of the head; only cost of acquisition is deductible; no other expenditure, allowance or set-off of loss is permitted.
Loss from transfer of a VDA cannot be set off against any income, including other VDA gains, and cannot be carried forward. "Transfer" applies to VDAs whether or not they are capital assets.
concepts.analogy: Thirty percent on gains, zero relief for losses.
concepts.work: A ₹1 lakh gain on one token and a ₹50,000 loss on another still leaves ₹1 lakh taxable.

concepts.title: TDS and gifts of virtual digital assets
body: Section 393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi): the payer for transfer of a VDA deducts tax at 1% of the consideration. Where consideration is in kind or exchanged for another VDA, the payer must ensure the tax is paid before releasing it.

No TDS is needed if consideration in the year does not exceed ₹50,000 where the payer is a specified person (individuals/HUFs with business turnover up to ₹1 crore or professional receipts up to ₹50 lakh, or with no business income) and ₹10,000 for others; specified persons need not obtain TAN. Where both the purchase-of-goods TDS and VDA TDS could apply, VDA TDS prevails.
Gifts of VDAs are "property" under section 92(2)(m): FMV taxable if aggregate exceeds ₹50,000 from non-relatives, with the usual exclusions (relatives, marriage, will).
concepts.analogy: Track 1% TDS on each trade and gift thresholds.
concepts.work: A ₹3 lakh token sale bears TDS of ₹3,000.

Equalisation levy withdrawn (2024) and abolished (Finance Act 2025).
VDA section 2(111); 30% tax; cost only; no loss set-off.
traps: Deducting exchange fees from VDA gains.

viva.q: Why are digital businesses hard to tax under PE rules?
viva.model: PE rules look for a fixed place of business or a dependent agent, while such firms earn from a market remotely.

viva.q: Which BEPS Action dealt with the digital economy?
viva.model: Action 1, which considered significant economic presence, withholding and an equalisation levy.

viva.q: What can be deducted from VDA transfer income?
Who must deduct tax on a VDA transfer?
viva.model: The person paying consideration to a resident for the transfer, at 1%.

viva.q: Does the gift provision apply to VDAs?
viva.model: Yes, VDAs are property for section 92(2)(m), with the usual exclusions.
